spec_notes: The spec (docs/shiploop/spec.md, R-1 to R-5) restates the request faithfully and contradicts it nowhere. It decides without marking: R-1 'The input contract is valid orthodox FEN' (silent on what happens otherwise, although the delivered code and README throw 'Invalid FEN:' for malformed input and answer impossible positions); R-2/R-3 'sorted lowercase UCI' and 'IllegalMoveError for other moves' (so upper case and whitespace are rejected); R-4 'The API provides no additional draw statuses'. It pins test content rather than behaviour (complete FEN comparisons, named TCs). It says nothing about IllegalMoveError's shape, inconsistent castling/en-passant fields, perft depth beyond what R-5 calls standard counts, or statelessness (the architecture note says 'FEN carries all state').
tests_notes: One file, 11 tests, several of which bundle many behaviours: TC-2 both mates; TC-3 (first) four castles plus three rights-loss cases; TC-4 (first) targets, clocks, white and black captures and expiry; TC-5 promotions plus a list of malformed and illegal move strings; TC-6 stalemate, check and a pin; TC-9 thirteen FENs across three functions. The exported-class check is fragile: with IllegalMoveError removed from the exports, every assert.throws(..., IllegalMoveError) passes (an undefined validator only checks that something threw) and only TC-9 fails, through a TypeError in its 'instanceof IllegalMoveError'. TC-9 pins the message prefix 'Invalid FEN' and the choice of a plain Error that is not IllegalMoveError, which another correct build (e.g. throwing IllegalMoveError or a TypeError for a bad FEN, both acceptable) would fail. TC-6 asserts the exact reply list for the check position and TC-1 the exact start list, which any correct build shares. TC-8 measures wall-clock time once (timing-dependent, but with a very wide margin: 0.07 ms against 50 ms). No test covers impossible positions, statelessness, or the error's name/message.
maintainer: All logic sits in one 355-line file on a 0x88 board, and the same boardAfter/legalCandidates helpers serve legal-move filtering, castling transit checks and applyMove, so a change to the move record (captureSquare, rookFrom/rookTo, promotion) ripples into all three. Castling rights loss is derived from the CASTLE_RIGHTS table by piece and square in rightsAfter, which is compact but easy to break for one corner without a dedicated test per corner; the perft tests at depth 3 are the main safety net.
